text:
Sam: FYI seeing a sharp p99 jump on s6-gpu pool after last night's driver rollout — model:/realtime/chat p99 ~45ms -> ~220ms, throughput down ~18%. Not steady-state, started ~02:10 UTC.
Maya: ouch. any noisy tenant or infra alerts?
Sam: No infra alerts. Instance-level metrics look normal but kernel launch latencies spiked and GPU SM util dropped during the periods. Logs attached from the request tracer.
Liam: grabbing perf traces now. initial look: kernel selection shifted to `flash_attn_v2` variant for short seqs (seq<=64) on many requests. That variant shows higher workspace alloc + launch latency on the new driver.
Jin: interesting — our KV-cache hit rate also dipped ~10% at same time for those models, so effective seq lengths increased -> different kernel path. Could be correlated.
Kevin: is this the CUDA driver 530.x roll? deploy-bot, can you confirm which driver batch went out at 02:00?
deploy-bot: driver-rollout-prod v530.12 applied to s6 pool at 01:58 UTC (canary -> 80% -> 100%). Link: https://deployments.redwood.local/rollouts/530.12
Liam: profiling snippet (short):
```
kernel: flash_attn_fwd_v2 size=48 workspace=1.2MB launch=0.2ms exec=0.45ms total=0.65ms
kernel: flash_attn_fwd_v2 size=64 workspace=2.4MB launch=0.9ms exec=4.8ms total=5.7ms
kernel: triton_gemm size=64 exec=0.9ms total=1.1ms
```
Liam: you can see a big jump at size=64 for this kernel on v530.
Maya: that exec jump explains p99. Why would kernel chooser flip to flash_attn for seq=64? Our selector uses cost model based on measured latency + workspace availability. Did workspace/query-alloc policies change?
Jin: KV cache dip probably raised observed seq lengths above the tiebreak. When prefix hits drop, requests include more tokens, pushing into different branch. Also noticed prefetch thrash in the allocator logs around same times.
Kevin: can we force the selector to prefer triton_gemm for short seqs as emergency mitigation? We have per-model overrides.
Sam: yes we can patch the routing table to set kernel_preference: [triton_gemm, flash_attn] for the chat models. That needs a hot-config and rollout.
ops-bot: Created incident INC-1977, auto-assign: eng-runtime oncall. Priority: P2. Suggested mitigations: rollback driver OR kernel-override.
Kevin: I can push a kernel_preference hot-config to the s6 fleet canary now, then 30m ramp if stable. Who owns verification?
Maya: I’ll validate p50/p99 and KV hit after canary. Liam pls attach full perf traces. Jin pls surface allocator/gc logs.
Liam: attaching flamegraphs + nvprof output to the incident: /incidents/1977/artifacts (large). Key takeaway: v530 increased kernel launch and sync overhead for flash_attn at certain workspace sizes.
Jin: allocator logs show more small async cudaMallocs and a spike in host->device memcpy stall times at same windows. Could be memory allocator ABI change in driver.
Sam: rollback path: ops can revert to v525 canary snapshot; but that will be disruptive. Prefer kernel override first and monitor 1 hour.
Kevin: doing canary patch now: pushing kernel_preference for model:/realtime/chat -> triton_gemm first. Rolling to 5% nodes.
Maya: saw initial canary p99 drop to ~60ms on those nodes. Need full 5-10 minute window to be confident.
Liam: also adding a temporary selector flag to log which branch decision was used per request to verify global flip rate.
Kevin: rolling to 30% now. ops-bot: tag me if any regression on other models.
ops-bot: Canary patch applied to 5% at 03:40 UTC, 30% at 03:52 UTC.
Sam: plan after verification: keep kernel override until driver vendor patches or until we adjust kernel cost model thresholds. Also open bug with vendor about workspace/launch behavior.
Jin: noted — I'll open INF-DRV-230 with traces and allocator logs.
Maya: summary for INC-1977: root cause likely driver v530 kernel/allocator behavior change that made flash_attn variant >5x slower for certain short-seq workspace sizes AND KV-cache hit rate dip nudged selector into that variant. Mitigation: kernel_preference override rolled; long-term: vendor engagement + adjust selector cost model to be more robust to transient KV hit changes.
Sam: thanks all. please keep updates short here, ping if rollback needed. :thumbsup:
